parts.text: In this experiment, you will investigate the heating of a thermometer bulb. Carry out the following instructions, referring to Figs. 2.1 and 2.2. Fig. 2.1 You are provided with a lamp and a rule. Do not move the lamp or the rule. During the experiment, you will read temperature values from the thermometer. You should use the card provided to shield your eyes from the direct rays of the lamp.

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Record the value of room temperature θ R shown on the thermometer. θ R = ................................................. [1]

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) Switch on the lamp. Leave the lamp switched on until you have completed all the readings.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Place the thermometer so that its bulb is a horizontal distance d = 100 mm from the surface of the lamp, as shown in Fig. 2.1. Record in Table 2.1 the distance d between the thermometer bulb and the surface of the lamp. Also record the temperature θ shown on the thermometer.

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Move the thermometer so that its bulb is a distance d = 80 mm from the surface of the lamp. In the table, record the distance d and the temperature θ . Table 2.1 d / θ /

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Repeat the steps described in (b)(ii) , but using values of d of 60 mm, 40 mm, 20 mm and 10 mm.

parts.label: iv
parts.text: (iv) Complete the column headings in the table. [4]

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) Move the thermometer away from the lamp and wait for about a minute for the thermometer to cool. Fig. 2.2

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Place the thermometer so that its bulb is a vertical distance d V = 100 mm from the top surface of the lamp, as shown in Fig. 2.2. Use the 100 mm rod provided to obtain the correct distance. Record the temperature θ V shown on the thermometer. θ V = ................................................. [1]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Calculate the difference between θ V and the thermometer reading θ H at a horizontal distance of 100 mm from the lamp. State whether θ V is higher, lower or the same as θ H . temperature difference = ...................................................... θ V is ................................................. [1]

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) A student suggests that θ V will be higher than the thermometer reading θ H because thermal energy will travel by infra-red radiation and convection to the thermometer bulb above the lamp but by infra-red radiation only when the bulb is to one side of the lamp. If the experiment were to be repeated in order to investigate this suggestion, it would be important to control the conditions. Suggest two such conditions, relevant to this investigation, that should be controlled. 1. ...................................................................................................................................... 2. ......................................................................................................................................
